# Run book: See what the API just did

[Run books](README.md) | [User guide](../user-guide/see-recent-traces.md) | [Spec](../specs/see-recent-traces.md)

## Contents

- [Purpose](#purpose)
- [Preconditions](#preconditions)
- [Verify](#verify)
- [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)

## Purpose

Traces and logs leave the service over OTLP, so any dashboard can show them; this page reads the latest back and links into the dashboard for the detail.

## Preconditions

- The compose stack is running, which includes the Aspire dashboard.

## Verify

Automatically: `npx playwright test e2e/journeys.spec.ts -g "See what the API just did"` (add `E2E_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8088` to run against the compose stack).

By hand, in the example web application at `/operations/telemetry`:

1. **Open the telemetry page.** The page loads the most recent traces on its own; use Refresh to reload them. Expect: A table lists recent spans with their duration and a trace link. A link opens the dashboard.

## Troubleshooting

**Table 1 — Known problems**

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No traces yet | Nothing has called the API since it started | Use another screen, then refresh |
| The dashboard could not be read | The API cannot reach the dashboard or the API key is wrong | Check Telemetry__DashboardUrl and Telemetry__ApiKey in the compose environment |

Related framework features: OoBDev.OpenTelemetry (OTLP export); Aspire dashboard telemetry API.
